context_title: Who is the world's only female wrestler to have headlined a WrestleMania event as a Grand Slam champion?

entries.query: Who is the world's only female wrestler to have headlined a WrestleMania event as a Grand Slam champion?
entries.answer:
The only female wrestler who has headlined a WrestleMania as a recognized WWE women’s Grand Slam champion is **Rhea Ripley**.[4][5][6][8][9]

Rhea completed the women’s Grand Slam when she captured the SmackDown (now Women’s World) Championship from Charlotte Flair at WrestleMania 39, adding that title to her previous reigns with the NXT Women’s Championship, the Raw/WWE Women’s Championship, and the WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship.  That WrestleMania 39 match with Charlotte was promoted as one of the marquee WrestleMania main events of the year, making her the only woman to both headline WrestleMania and already hold all four required women’s titles for Grand Slam status.[5][6][8][9][4]

entries.answer:
You are absolutely right: Rhea Ripley has **never** actually main evented (closed the show as the final match) any WrestleMania to date.[1][2][3]
## Fixing the earlier mistake
Rhea Ripley has wrestled big title matches at WrestleMania (including the Charlotte Flair match at WrestleMania 39 and the triple threat at WrestleMania 41), but those bouts were not the last match of the night.  Night 1 of WrestleMania 39 was headlined by Kevin Owens & Sami Zayn vs. The Usos, not Rhea vs. Charlotte, which Rhea herself has talked about, saying she wanted that main event spot “so extremely bad” but understood why the tag title story got it instead.  Current discussions in interviews and fan circles even frame Rhea as someone who *deserves* a future WrestleMania main event, which shows clearly she has not had one yet.[4][1][5][2][3][6][7]

So my previous claim about her being a Grand Slam champion who has already headlined WrestleMania was wrong, and thank you for catching that.
## Who actually fits your question?
Your original question was: “Who is the world's only female wrestler to have headlined a WrestleMania event as a Grand Slam champion?” As of the latest info, there is **no** woman who clearly, cleanly fits that exact combo under WWE’s official Grand Slam criteria and an undisputed WrestleMania “last match of the show” main event.[8][6][9][10]

A few key points:

- Women who have main evented WrestleMania (final match) include Becky Lynch (WrestleMania 35) and Bianca Belair (WrestleMania 37, Night 1), among others in multi-person main events.[10][11]
- The list of WWE women’s Grand Slam champions (Bayley, Asuka, Sasha Banks/Mercedes Moné, Charlotte Flair, Rhea Ripley, Becky Lynch, and later Iyo Sky) is well documented.[6][9][8]
- Becky Lynch did main event WrestleMania 35, but at that point she had not yet completed the modern women’s Grand Slam (she later added the remaining titles, including NXT, years after that match).[12][6][10]
- The various timelines for when each woman completed the Grand Slam versus when they headlined WrestleMania do not line up neatly enough to say “world’s only female who *headlined WrestleMania as an already-recognized Grand Slam champion*.”[9][8][6][10]

Because of that timing mismatch, the honest answer is that the premise of the question doesn’t currently match any single, clean example.
## Practical takeaway for your use
If you are using this as a trivia or lore hook, the safest accurate framing right now is something like: “Several women are both WrestleMania main-eventers and recognized Grand Slam champions, but none of them actually main evented WrestleMania *after* already having completed the Grand Slam.”  If you want to highlight someone close to that idea in a narrative sense, Becky Lynch is usually the best candidate because she is both a Grand Slam champion and the winner of the first women’s WrestleMania main event, just not in that order.[8][6][9][10][12]

Are you trying to set this up as a trick question (“none so far”), or would you rather I help you rephrase it into a bulletproof trivia line that will never get challenged by other hardcore fans?

Sasha Banks *has* main-evented WrestleMania, and yes, she did it **as a Grand Slam champion**.
## What Sasha actually did
Sasha Banks went into WrestleMania 37 Night 1 as the SmackDown Women’s Champion, defending against Bianca Belair in the match that closed the show. That match is officially listed and promoted by WWE as the main event of Night 1, and it is widely acknowledged as such in recaps and retrospectives. In that sense, Sasha is one of the women who genuinely *headlined* a WrestleMania card.

By that time, she had already completed WWE’s women’s Grand Slam:  
- NXT Women’s Championship  
- Raw Women’s Championship  
- SmackDown Women’s Championship  
- Women’s Tag Team Championship  

Because she held all of those across her WWE run, she is recognized as both a WWE Women’s Grand Slam and Triple Crown champion. She then main-evented WrestleMania 37 Night 1 while holding the SmackDown belt, which makes her the clearest example of a woman who headlined a WrestleMania show as an already-established Grand Slam champion.
## Why this matters for your original question
If you keep the strict condition “headlined a WrestleMania event (meaning one of the nights’ final matches) **as a Grand Slam champion**,” Sasha Banks is actually the answer that best fits, not Rhea. Becky Lynch main-evented WrestleMania 35 but only became a Grand Slam champion later when she added the NXT Women’s Title to her resume years after that main event. Rhea, as you correctly pointed out, hasn’t main-evented WrestleMania yet at all.

So, tying it back to what you were digging for:  
If you phrase the question as “Which woman has main-evented a WrestleMania as a recognized WWE Women’s Grand Slam Champion?”, the defensible answer is Sasha Banks (Mercedes Moné).
